key_insight: SkillOpt dramatically improved false-presupposition correction in cancer-related LLM responses, but the gains were model-dependent and could increase over-correction.
clinical_relevance: For cancer communication tools, prompts should be validated on each target model because better correction of misleading assumptions can come with reduced accuracy on valid questions.
method: Used the physician-verified Cancer-Myth benchmark with 117 FP training questions, 58 FP + 30 NFP validation questions, and 410 unseen FP test questions.
Compared no correction, a strong seven-example few-shot prompt, GPT-5.4-generated instruction-only prompts, and full/compact SkillOpt skills across seven LLMs.
A separate GPT-4o model judged outputs, and performance was evaluated with bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm-adjusted significance testing.
evidence_signal: Across GPT-4o, SkillOpt raised FP correction from 15.4-17.6% to 82.2-90.5% with 95% bootstrap CIs and all Holm-adjusted p<0.001, while compact SkillOpt improved NFP accuracy on capable models.
watch_item: The method was not universally portable and sometimes over-corrected valid clinical assumptions, so it needs model-specific testing before deployment.
paper_title: Automated Skill Optimisation for False Presupposition Handling in Cancer Communication: SkillOpt Versus Conventional Prompt Engineering Across Language Models
